To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the spontaneously hypertensiv rat on a high-salt diet the aggravated development of high blood pressure was associated with an increased blood pressure and heart-rate response to ganglion blockade but no major changes in central adrenoceptor mediated functions and neuronal activity of brain-stem NA neurons.
the enhanced blood pressure response to phenylephine in the spontaneously hyperten-sive rat is not due to changes in central adrenergics.

in the spontaneously hypertensitive rat on a high-salt diet the aggravated development of the hypertension is not associated with major alterations in central alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenoceptor mediated functions and neuronal activity of brainstem noradrenergic neurons, whereas the basal sympathetic tone may be increased and the blood pressure response to vasoconstrictor substances enhanced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic salt intake on central adrenergetic mechanisms in the spontaneously hyperensive rat.
the effects of chronic salt intake on the development and maintenance of hypertension.
the effects of salt loading in the spontaneously hypertensiv e rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the central noradrenergic system is not a primary cause of the increased blood pressure in spontaneously hypertensive rat maintained on a high salt diet.
the central adrenergically mediated mechanisms are not of importance for the development of hypertension in this model.
central alpha 1- and alpha 2-receptors are not implicated in the genesis or development of salt induced hypertension in spontaneously hypertensive animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic salt loading in the spontaneously hypertense rat is associated with increased sympathetic outflow and an increased peripheral responsiveness to sympathetic stimuli but not with alterations in central adrenergically mediated functions.
the increased blood pressure in spontaneously hypertensive rat following a salt load is due to a peripheral mechanism, probably increased peripheral alpha 1-adrenergic responsiveness.
central alpha 1- and alpha 2- adrenoceptor mediated functions are not important for the development of the spontaneously hypertensive hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the increased blood pressure response in spontaneously hypertensive rat to pressor substances was not due to changes in adrenoceptor sensitivity or central NA neuronal activity but may be due to a higher basal sympathetic tone.
salt loading in SHR does not alter the central adrenergics, and that this is a good animal model to study the effects of salt on the periphery.
salt intake can have an impact on blood pressure and the sympathetic nervous system, and that this impact may be mediated by central alpha 2 adrenergic receptors.
